response.title: Muslim Quarter: a short history
response.summary: The Muslim Quarter is the largest of the Old City's four traditional quarters.
response.narrative:
The Muslim Quarter is the largest of the Old City's four traditional quarters. Its residential lanes, schools, places of worship and markets extend from Bab al-Amud toward the Haram al-Sharif/Al-Aqsa compound.

Mamluk era (1250-1517 CE): Major madrasas, ribats, markets and residential buildings were endowed and constructed along approaches to Al-Aqsa.
Ottoman era (1517-1917 CE): Existing religious and commercial institutions continued, while the quarter remained a major centre of Old City life.

Main landmarks:
- Bab Hutta.
- Via Dolorosa.
- Souq al-Qattanin.
- Mamluk madrasas along the western edge of Al-Aqsa.
